# iwe bare front matter support

## Problem

iwe requires `---` fenced YAML front matter. Some wiki systems (e.g., TibbitWiki) use bare RFC 822-style headers — `key: value` lines at the top of the file, separated from body by a blank line, no delimiters. The content is valid YAML; only the framing differs.

## Design

### Detection rule

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled in config and the file does not start with `---`:
- Check if the first line starts with `title: `
- If so, all lines up to the first blank line are treated as front matter
- Parse that block as YAML

If the first line is not `title: `, no bare front matter is detected; the file is parsed normally.

The `title:` requirement avoids false positives (e.g., prose starting with `Something: explanation`). No key whitelist is needed — `title` as a mandatory first key is sufficient, and additional keys can be added freely over time.

### Config

Add `bare_frontmatter = true` to `.iwe/config.toml` under `[markdown]`. Default: `false` (current behavior preserved).

### Reader changes

In `MarkdownReader::document()` (or the events reader), before passing content to pulldown_cmark:
- If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled, detect bare headers per the rule above
- Wrap the detected block with `---` delimiters so pulldown_cmark parses it as a metadata block
- The rest of the pipeline (metadata storage, title extraction, graph) works unchanged

### Writer changes

If `bare_frontmatter` is enabled:
- Emit metadata as bare `key: value` lines followed by a blank line — no `---` fences
- This preserves round-trip compatibility with systems that don't understand YAML front matter delimiters

### Scope of changes

- `crates/liwe/src/model/config.rs` — add `bare_frontmatter` field
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs` or `crates/liwe/src/markdown/reader.rs` — pre-process content
- `crates/liwe/src/markdown/writer.rs` — conditional fence suppression
- Tests for: detection, round-trip, no false positive on prose, interaction with `---` fenced files

## Future: metadata querying

Once front matter is reliably parsed (bare or fenced), add `--meta key=value` filtering to `iwe find`. This enables task tracking via front matter fields like `status: active`, `depends: concurrency-design`, etc., queryable from the CLI.

## Compatibility note

TibbitWiki uses four keys: `title`, `tags`, `created`, `modified`. Enabling `bare_frontmatter` in an iwe workspace pointing at wiki notes would let iwe read them natively. The writer would emit bare headers, preserving compatibility with the wiki.

data.deltaContent: I
found the issue—the `wrap_bare_frontmatter` function is filtering out any lines that start with whitespace, but YAML sequences use
indentation with hyphens like `  - foo`, so those lines get
stripped out and the sequence data disappears from the metadata entirely.
Now
I need to understand why that filter exists in the first place, then write
a test to confirm the bug before fixing it.
Found the bug. In `wrap_bare_frontmatter` in `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`

, the code filters out lines starting with a space:

```rust
.filter(|l| !l.starts_with(' '))
```

This drops YAML sequence items like

`  - foo` (the typical indented YAML list syntax), so:

```
title: ...
depends:
  - foo
```

bec

omes:

```
title: ...
depends:
```

losing the sequence values entirely. Let me confirm and write a test.

## Summary

**Root cause:**
In `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, the `wrap_bare_

frontmatter` function "cleaned" the detected header block by filtering out any line starting with a space:

```rust
.filter(|l| !l.starts_with(' '))
```

That
filter silently dropped indented YAML lines — exactly the form used by standard YAML sequences:

```
title: Task A
depends:
  - foo
```

After the fil
ter, the metadata seen by the rest of the pipeline became `"title: Task A\
ndepends:\n"` (an empty `depends` field), so `iwe find --meta depends=
foo` never matched. Fenced (`---`) front matter doesn't go through `wrap_bare_frontmatter`, which is why it

worked there.

**Fix:** Removed the line-filtering. The header span is already corre
ctly bounded by the first blank line, so every line in that span belongs to the YAML front matter and must be preserved verbatim. The
`\n---\n` fences are now wrapped around the original header (with `trim_end`

to avoid trailing whitespace).

**Verification:**
- Added regression test `value_in_yaml_sequence_matches_bare_frontmatter` in `crates/

liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs` — fails before the fix, passes after.
- Full `cargo test` pass
es with 0 failures.

## Summary

**Root cause:** In `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, the `wrap_bare_frontmatter` function "cleaned" the detected header block by filtering out any line starting with a space:

```rust
.filter(|l| !l.starts_with(' '))
```

That filter silently dropped indented YAML lines — exactly the form used by standard YAML sequences:

```
title: Task A
depends:
  - foo
```

After the filter, the metadata seen by the rest of the pipeline became `"title: Task A\ndepends:\n"` (an empty `depends` field), so `iwe find --meta depends=foo` never matched. Fenced (`---`) front matter doesn't go through `wrap_bare_frontmatter`, which is why it worked there.

**Fix:** Removed the line-filtering. The header span is already correctly bounded by the first blank line, so every line in that span belongs to the YAML front matter and must be preserved verbatim. The `\n---\n` fences are now wrapped around the original header (with `trim_end` to avoid trailing whitespace).

**Verification:**
- Added regression test `value_in_yaml_sequence_matches_bare_frontmatter` in `crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs` — fails before the fix, passes after.
